title: The Case of the Missing Birthday Cake

characters.role: the reader / main character, a clever kid detective
the family dog who loves sniffing out clues

coverMeta.personalizedTitle: Detective Alex and the Missing Birthday Cake

pages.text:
The party balloons are up, the candles are ready, but the big birthday cake has vanished from the kitchen counter. "A mystery!" you gasp, snapping on your detective cap.

Your sidekick Sam grabs a magnifying glass, and the dog Pip wags a helpful tail. Time to crack the case.

choices.text: Search for a trail of crumbs

pages.text:
You spot little smudges of frosting near the counter, shaped like tiny fingertips. "A clue!" whispers Sam, writing it in the notebook.

The smudges lead in two directions, one toward the humming fridge and one toward the open window.

A line of soft cake crumbs trails across the floor like a dotted path. Pip sniffs each one with a curious wet nose.

The crumbs split at the hallway, one path leading to the sunny garden and one to the cozy living room.

choices.text: Follow the crumbs to the garden
Follow the crumbs to the living room

pages.text:
Here you find a surprising clue: a single fuzzy slipper print pressed into a dusting of flour. "Whoever took the cake was wearing comfy slippers," you note.

Pip barks and points a paw toward the backyard, while your little cousin peeks around the corner with a grin.

choices.text: Follow the paw toward the backyard
Ask your grinning cousin what they saw

pages.text:
You discover a sprinkle of rainbow candy bits and a tiny folded note. The note says, "Just making sure it tastes perfect."

"Very suspicious," says Sam. The sprinkles lead toward the garden shed and toward Grandpa's comfy reading chair.

Outside in the warm sun, you spot the cake sitting safe on a low table, with only one tiny nibble missing from the corner. Nearby, Pip has a smudge of frosting right on that fuzzy nose.

"The case is warming up," you giggle. But something tells you there is more to this sweet mystery.

choices.text: Sneak closer for a better look

pages.text:
Your cousin points toward the porch, where a trail of powdered sugar leads to a big striped picnic blanket. Something lumpy is hiding underneath.

You tiptoe closer and hear a soft, happy humming sound. "We have almost solved it," you whisper to Sam.

You lift the corner and find Grandpa sitting with the cake on his lap, a tiny spoon in hand. "I was only checking the frosting," he laughs, "to make sure it was perfect for the party."

He did not eat much at all, just a wee taste, and the cake is still beautiful. Everyone bursts into giggles.

choices.text: Laugh and carry the cake back inside
Make Grandpa an honorary taste tester

pages.text:
Everyone gathers around, and the truth comes out with lots of laughing. Pip took one gentle nibble, and Grandpa carried the cake outside for a secret taste test, both of them just too excited for the party.

The cake is safe, the frosting is perfect, and the mystery is solved. Detective work is delicious.

choices.text: Forgive Pip with a big hug
Bake a little extra treat together

pages.text:
You carry the cake back to the table like a true hero, and everyone claps for the great detective. The candles are lit, and the whole family sings a happy birthday song.

Grandpa promises to wait for the party next time, with a twinkle in his eye. Best case ever. The end.

You pin a shiny paper badge on your shirt and one on Sam too. Grandpa gets the official title of Chief Frosting Tester, which he wears with great pride.

Everyone agrees it was the silliest, sweetest mystery of the year. The end.

You give Pip a big forgiving hug and pop a tiny party hat right between those fuzzy ears. The frosting bandit wags a happy tail and licks your cheek.

Everyone poses for a photo with the rescued cake. Case closed, hearts full. The end.

To celebrate cracking the case, you and Sam help bake a second little cake, just for fun. You swirl the frosting and toss on a rainbow of sprinkles.

Now there is plenty of cake for everyone, even the very hungry helpers. Sharing is the sweetest ending of all. The end.
